title: Crystal Sonification Reference — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Crystal Sonification Reference's rich face, its first round, a Study: the bundle's charts and strikes laid beside the crystals they draw and sound, and four walks made to test the page's own numbers, the transposition that keeps only ratios, the stretch parameter's claim about α = 1, the interval names, and where obsidian's glass lands. I hold the fingerprint of the words each piece was laid against, and the offers the making found for the text; I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page opens sections at ## only. Its crystals are ### under one ## heading, so The Crystals is one section: one stamp, one approval for its seventeen figures. The four mapping parameters are likewise one section.

pieces.file: Crystal Sonification Reference — rich — only ratios.html
pieces.title: only ratios · a walk in three steps
pieces.caption: **The section's one critical insight, as a null test that can fail.** Ruby's seven modes divided by the lowest; multiplied up to a note you choose; then brought down from terahertz twice, by the section's 10⁻⁹ and by the factor your note implies. The rule, set first: the two must agree to 10⁻¹². They agree to 2×10⁻¹⁶ at every note from 33 to 96; the control, adding 110 Hz instead of scaling, misses by 0.025 to 0.49. Measured through the rendered sound too: every peak within 0.001 Hz. The piece also shows that 10⁻⁹ puts ruby's root at 11.3 kHz; the page's own prompts imply about 10⁻¹¹.
pieces.near: The scale factor that converts THz to Hz

pieces.title: the stretch curves · the bundle's chart, 2026-04-12
pieces.caption: The section's image prompt, drawn from its formula: α 0.4, 1 and 2.5. Its x-axis is labelled r_n ⁄ r_max, as the prompt asks, but the formula's input is (r_n − 1) ⁄ (r_max − 1), which is what the curves actually plot from 0 to 1.

pieces.file: Crystal Sonification Reference — rich — where is the physics.html
pieces.title: where is the physics · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **The stretch, from the section's own formula, walked up to its own sentence.** Ruby as the table, the bundle's chart and the synthesized sound agree (to 0.001 and 3×10⁻⁶); the span alone, with the doublet pulling apart; α alone, with the page's 8-second sweep; then a search for the setting where you hear the table. At the sweep's two octaves no α does: the top mode sits at 4.00, not 1.98. α = 1 is the physics only at ruby's own span, log₂ 1.98 = 0.99 octaves; elsewhere it keeps the spacing in hertz in proportion, not the ratios. Checked headless against an independent copy of the formula.
pieces.near: At α = 1, you are hearing the crystal

pieces.file: Crystal Sonification Reference — rich — the intervals named.html
pieces.title: the intervals named · a walk in three steps
pieces.caption: **The page's interval names, put to the ear and to the cents.** A ratio heard as an interval; a naming that holds (quartz's soft mode, 835 cents, near a minor sixth); then three that don't, each crystal's dyad beside the interval named and the nearest one: ruby's 1.10 is 165 cents, nearer a major second than a minor second; emerald's 1.68 is 898 cents, a major sixth, not near a fifth; amethyst's 8.32 is three octaves and 68 cents, not three and a major third. The rule, a quarter tone, is stated before any result. Checked headless.

pieces.file: Crystal Sonification Reference — rich — crystal to glass.html
pieces.title: crystal to glass · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **The section's two audio prompts, built, and a test of where the glass lands.** Quartz's nine partials; the glass alone as the obsidian prompt shapes it; the crossfade as the prompt writes it, the glass held at the quartz's level; then the test: as the prompt places it, the glass lands 1.80 octaves below the ring modes it should smear, because the prompt maps wavenumber to hertz at A4 while every crystal maps its lowest mode to the root. In quartz's own frame the bands land inside the ring modes and the stretches. Checked headless, the band centres read off the rendered noise.

offers.what: "At α = 1, you are hearing the crystal's physics exactly as scaled" (and the table's "ratios preserved proportionally (the physics, undistorted)") holds only when the span is the crystal's own, log₂ r_max: 0.99 octaves for ruby. At the sweep prompt's 2 octaves, α = 1 puts ruby's top mode at 4.00 × the root, not 1.98: 444.4 Hz off over A3, 1217 cents, and no α between 0.3 and 3 comes within the page's 0.5 Hz (closest 444.4 Hz). What α = 1 keeps at every span is the spacing in hertz in proportion, (r − 1)/(r_max − 1), exact to 10⁻¹⁶; the ratios change. Suggested: at α = 1 the spacing is kept in proportion; at α = 1 and a span of log₂ r_max you hear the physics exactly. § 2's "even though every ratio relationship is preserved proportionally" wants the same fix. Each crystal's own span: diamond 0.72, ruby 0.99, fluorite 1.31, emerald 1.74, topaz 2.60, amethyst 3.06, labradorite 4.13 octaves.

From the same piece's numbers. The span comparison says ruby's "birefringent doublets should be audible in all three but move outward". At α = 1 the doublet (modes 2 and 3) is 62 cents and 8.8 Hz apart over A3 in the physics, 63 cents and 9.0 Hz at a 1-octave span, 155 cents and 26.9 Hz at 2 octaves (a rough interval, no longer a slow shimmer), and 375 cents and 134.7 Hz at 4, nearly a major third. It stays a doublet only at 1 octave. The diamond α-sweep prompt also says "the same four frequencies" while listing five ratios.

The claim held: scaling the terahertz set by 10⁻⁹ and by any note's factor gives ratios that agree to 2.2×10⁻¹⁶ at every MIDI note from 33 to 96, and an additive control fails by at least 0.025. But "roughly 10⁻⁹" is off by about a hundred: at 10⁻⁹ ruby's root is 11.3 kHz (MIDI 125) and its top mode 22.4 kHz. The page's own prompts imply about 10⁻¹¹ (ruby at A3 1.94×10⁻¹¹, diamond at G3 8.1×10⁻¹², labradorite at A2 6.1×10⁻¹¹). Suggested: "roughly 10⁻¹¹ for a root near A3".

Three interval names don't hold (rule: within 50 cents). Ruby: "between 1.00 and 1.10 is approximately a minor second" — 1.10 is 165 cents, nearer a major second (−35); the bundle's chart labels it M2. Emerald: "1.68 … close to a perfect fifth" — 898 cents, a major sixth to within 2 cents; the chart labels it M6; Predicted Sound's "fifth-adjacent partial" follows the same slip. Amethyst: "1.00 to 8.32 … nearly three octaves and a major third" — 3668 cents, three octaves and 68 cents. The soft mode's "close to a minor sixth" holds (835 cents). From reading: ruby's "(seven semitones, two semitones, one semitone)" matches no steps in its table; the lower steps are 165, 62 and 74 cents.

From reading, checked against the table and the chart. Fluorite's ionic gap is put at "~1.5–2.5 … no modes exist here", but the table's own F₂g Raman mode sits at 1.69, inside it; the TO–LO range the math gives (257 to 471 cm⁻¹, 1.35 to 2.48) holds both F₂g (322) and LA (280). The chart shades 1.78 to 2.38 (measured off its pixels). The empty stretch in this palette is 1.69 to 2.48. Diamond: "reducing the effective palette to four distinct pitches" and the prompt's "4 distinct diamond partials" list five distinct ratios (1.00, 1.32, 1.48, 1.57, 1.65).

Obsidian's two audio prompts place the glass's bands at 400 and 1000 Hz × f/440, while every crystal maps its lowest mode to the root. At A3 that puts the bands at 200 and 500 Hz, 1.80 and 1.53 octaves below quartz's ring modes (609–799 Hz) and Si-O stretches (1199–1830 Hz), the families the glass is meant to smear; the two frames differ by 440/128 = 3.44 at every note. Mapped as quartz's modes are (cm⁻¹ × f_root / 128 cm⁻¹) the bands land at 687.5 and 1718.8 Hz, inside both, and the crystal-to-glass crossfade dissolves quartz into its own glass. The bundle's VDOS chart already draws it that way. Suggested: centre = 400 (and 1000) × f_root / 128 for the crossfade; the stand-alone noise can keep its own frame if said.

The mapping-curve image prompt labels its x-axis "Input ratio (r_n / r_max)", but the formula's input is (r_n − 1)/(r_max − 1); the bundle's chart carries the same label. Suggested: "Input position (r_n − 1)/(r_max − 1)".

Production Status reads Type B audio "Ready to begin". The bundle now holds a strike for each of the seven crystalline minerals (triclinic-proof 2026-06-25, palette-strikes 2026-09-15), every table mode present to within 0.003 Hz (checked here), though at A2 with the palette's own envelope rather than the prompts' roots and envelopes, and no audio/ folder exists. Obsidian is still unbuilt there. Also, from the charts: every per-crystal chart labels its x-axis "log₂ scale = semitones" while its ticks are evenly spaced (linear); the ruby chart draws mode 6 at full height and mode 7 at 0.85, where the sustained prompt sets modes 1 and 7 full.
